text.p: Bulgaria's Foreign Minister Georgi Pirinski, a prominent critic of Prime Minister Zhan Videnov, resigned on Wednesday, state radio said.
His resignation came a day after a meeting of the ruling Socialists gave their backing to Videnov in a confidence vote by a narrow margin.
The Constitutional Court barred Pirinski from running for the presidency in elections last month because he was not born in Bulgaria.
The defeat of the Socialists' eventual candidate, Culture Minister Ivan Marazov, widened rifts within the party and prompted fresh calls for policy reforms and a new cabinet.
Pirinski is often cited as a potential challenger to Videnov for the prime minister's job.
The radio quoted Videnov as saying he would name a new foreign minister by the end of next month and one of Pirinski's deputies would carry out his duties until then under the premier's supervision.
